questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the key difference between a data standard and a metadata standard?
options: A data standard governs the data values themselves; a metadata standard governs how you describe the data
They are two names for the exact same thing
A data standard only applies to numbers, a metadata standard only applies to text
Metadata standards are optional, while data standards are always legally mandatory
questions.explain: A data standard might require account numbers to be 10 digits; a metadata standard requires every glossary entry to have a name, definition, owner, and status.

questions.q: What is the most widely cited standard for structuring metadata registries, per this lesson?
options: ISO/IEC 11179
HTTP/2
ISO 8601
RFC 822
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 11179, 'Information technology — Metadata registries,' is the reference standard this lesson covers for structuring data element metadata.

questions.q: In ISO/IEC 11179's data element model, which three parts combine to fully specify a data element?
options: Object class, property, and representation
Table name, column name, and index name
Owner, steward, and custodian
Primary key, foreign key, and unique constraint
questions.explain: Object class (the real-world thing, like Customer), property (the characteristic, like Date of Birth), and representation (how it's stored) together form one unambiguous data element.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the six core fields this lesson says a standardized metadata entry should have?
options: Name and definition
Owner and status
Last reviewed date
The exact dollar cost of the storage hardware used
questions.explain: The six core fields are name, definition, data type/representation, owner/steward, status, and last-reviewed date — storage hardware cost isn't one of them.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does ISO/IEC 11179 not mandate specific values for data elements?
options: It mandates which fields a complete metadata record should have and how they relate, not the specific values themselves
Because the standard only applies to European organizations
Because specific values change too often to standardize
Because it is purely a technical formatting standard with no business relevance
questions.explain: The standard is about structure and completeness of metadata records (object class, property, representation), not about dictating what any individual organization's actual values must be.
